data.cultural_impact: The name Bhura in Hindu culture was used to signify the protection and blessings of the deity Vayu, the Hindu god of wind. Bhura is considered to be the benevolent and powerful guardian who keeps the balance of nature in check and also brings the essence of the wind to the world, thus ensuring prosperity and good fortune for people. This name was also used to describe individuals who exhibited such qualities and were considered holy and sacred.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Bhura holds significant meaning as it represents the divinity of the wind and the power of the gods. This name signifies the purifying and cleansing influence of the wind and the divine blessings of the gods, which are essential for the well-being and progress of humanity. It also represents the idea of being a spiritual guardian and protector, providing comfort and strength to those in need. The name Bhura thus embodies the essence of both the divine and the natural world and encourages us to strive for spiritual growth and connection with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Bhura was a king of the Yadava dynasty, who ruled over the region of Mathura in the 12th century CE.
historical_references.context: The Yadava kings were descendants of Krishna, and Mathura was the birthplace and childhood home of Krishna.

historical_references.reference: Bhura was also a renowned Hindu saint, who is believed to have lived during the medieval period, around the 16th century CE. He was a disciple of the saint Tulsidas, and is famous for his devotion to the deity Hanuman.
historical_references.context: Bhura is revered in the Hindu tradition, and his life and teachings continue to inspire and influence many people.
